_about: H74: the get-started tutorial. The call page shows these pieces on its real screens (the question mark at the top left); the demo call (app/tour.py) reads the same text, so both say the same. Demo content only: nothing here is anyone's real life. {donna} and {pepper} become the names of this HQ's agents.
intro: HQ is your own headquarters. You call your team, and they don't just answer: they write things down, plan your days and do the work. Pick a short piece below to see where everything is, or try a demo call and ask anything.
demo_note: Demo: everything in this tutorial is made-up example content. Nothing you tap here changes your HQ, and nothing is saved.

pieces.title: Call your team
pieces.line: Who you call, and how a call works

steps.title: Pick who you call
steps.text: {donna} is quick: your day, your list, your mail, quick orders. {pepper} takes her time: planning, sparring, thinking something through. Each has her own voice and character.

steps.title: Tap to call
steps.text: One tap and she picks up. Talk the way you would on the phone. You can cut in at any moment and she stops talking.

steps.title: Take it back
steps.text: Said something you didn't mean, or she heard you wrong? On a call, Cancel takes back what you just said, before she acts on it. She asks once to be sure.

steps.title: Mute, or hold to talk
steps.text: On a call this button mutes you with a tap. Hold it down to talk as long as you like, even with long pauses; let go and she answers.

steps.title: What she's doing
steps.text: This line says it: listening, thinking, talking. While she thinks you hear a soft tick, never silence.

items: Three things. The dentist at ten, a call with Alex at two, and the report you wanted done before Friday.

pieces.title: The chat, and typing instead
pieces.line: Read back what was said, or type when you can't talk

steps.title: What was said
steps.text: The chat shows the whole call as text, as it happens. Lists and bold words show there; she never reads the marks out loud.

steps.title: Type instead of talking
steps.text: On a train or in a library? Type in the chat's box and she answers out loud and in the chat. After a call, Call back and continue picks up right where you were.

items: Remind me to buy coffee tomorrow
Done. I'll text you tomorrow morning at nine.

steps.title: Mute her voice
steps.text: Turns her voice off and on, for when you'd rather read. She keeps answering in the chat.

pieces.title: Your to-do list, the Eisenhower way
pieces.line: Everything to do, sorted by what really matters

steps.title: One list for everything
steps.text: Everything you have to do lives here, in four squares: important or not, urgent or not. Important but not urgent comes first, because that's where the things that really move your life forward are.

steps.title: You just talk
steps.text: Keeping a list like this is usually a lot of admin. In HQ you just say it on a call or in a text: it lands in the right square, in your own words. Done or let go, and it moves, with a line so you can look back.

items: Learn to cook three new dishes · Plan the summer trip
Pay the tax bill by Friday

steps.title: Tap to work with it
steps.text: Tap a square for its list, an item for everything about it. Tick it off, move it, let it go, rename it, add one by hand, or start a call about it. Drag the dots at the start of a row to put it higher or lower in its list. Undo puts the last change back.

pieces.title: Texts with {donna}
pieces.line: Reminders, check-ins, and texting her yourself

steps.title: Her own text line
steps.text: {donna} texts you reminders at the time you asked, check-ins, and a heads-up when something needs you. You can text her back here like any chat app, and she does what you ask.

items: Morning. Dentist at ten, leave by half nine.
Thanks! Move my gym to tonight?

pieces.title: Your calendar
pieces.line: Your days at a glance, planned on a call

steps.title: Your days
steps.text: Your Google Calendar inside HQ: today and the days ahead. Ask on a call to plan your week, move something or block time, and she does it.

steps.title: Notes and calls on an appointment
steps.text: Tap an appointment for its details, a quick note of your own, or a call about it. Your own calendar she just changes; anything with other people in it, she checks with you first.

steps.title: Travel to an appointment
steps.text: An appointment away from home gets its trip by public transport by itself, once HQ knows where it is: its place in the calendar, or a friend's address you gave once. It starts at home, or where you are just before. In the hours before, HQ watches the live train, bus and tram data, and {donna} texts you when your train is cancelled, late or on another platform, or a stop near you has a message, with a 9292 link to plan again. Tap Travel in the appointment to turn it on or off.

items: Train from the station near home, there 13:39

pieces.title: Driving to appointments
pieces.line: By car, with the traffic, on your own maps key

steps.title: Driving to an appointment
steps.text: If you drive, a trip can go by car instead. HQ works out how long the drive takes with the traffic and when to leave. From two hours before, it keeps an eye on the traffic, and {donna} texts you when it's time to go, and again when the drive gets ten minutes longer or shorter. It opens in Google Maps. It's its own switch, off until you turn it on.

items: Leave by 13:15: 35 minutes by car, 8 of it traffic
{donna}: time to get going, leave by 13:15

steps.title: Your own maps key
steps.text: The traffic comes from a maps service, and HQ has no key of its own: you make your own, once, and it stays on your computer. Two kinds work. Google Maps asks for a card on file, but its free monthly use covers one person's trips many times over. TomTom is free without a card. Pick either; the next two pieces walk you through them.

steps.title: A Google Maps key, step by step
steps.text: 1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and sign in with your Google account. 2. At the top, make a new project, called HQ for example. 3. Open Billing and add a card (Google asks for it; the free use covers HQ). Under Budgets and alerts, set a small budget, like 5 euros, so you hear it if anything ever costs money. 4. Open APIs and Services, Library, search for Routes API, and press Enable. 5. Open APIs and Services, Credentials, Create credentials, API key. 6. Press Edit on the new key: under API restrictions pick Restrict key and tick only the Routes API, then Save. 7. Copy the key: it starts with AIza.

steps.title: Or TomTom, free without a card
steps.text: 1. Go to developer.tomtom.com and press Register. 2. Fill in your name and email, and confirm the email they send. 3. Sign in: your dashboard already has a key, on the Keys page. 4. Copy it. The free plan gives 2,500 looks a day; HQ uses about a dozen per trip and never more than 150 a day.

steps.title: Paste it in
steps.text: Open Settings, What HQ helps you with, and turn on Driving to appointments. A box shows up under it: paste your key and press Save. It's kept on this computer only, never in your workspace and never uploaded; the page only shows which kind it is. Running two HQs, a main and a backup? Paste it on each. Forget takes it off again. Never say or type your key on a call or in a text.

steps.title: On each appointment
steps.text: Open an appointment away from home and tap Travel. With only driving on, every trip is by car; with public transport on too, the trip starts by public transport and Go by car instead switches it. You can also just say it on a call: go by car to the dentist.

steps.title: A quick note
steps.text: A thought you don't want to lose? Write it here. The next call reads your notes, so you can say: let's go through my notes.

items: Ask about the new running shoes
Idea: a picnic in the park

pieces.title: Past calls
pieces.line: Every call, kept, to read back or continue

steps.title: Every call kept
steps.text: Every call is saved as text. Open one to read it back, or tap Continue this call, and she picks up where you left off, knowing what was said.

pieces.title: The team works while you're away
pieces.line: Agree work on a call, hang up, it gets done

steps.title: Give it to the team
steps.text: On a call you can agree a bigger piece of work: build something, sort something out, research something. Say: give it to the team. You hang up, and the computer does it by itself, one piece at a time.

steps.title: Watch how far it is
steps.text: The Status page shows what's being done right now and its step, what's waiting, what's planned for later, and your Claude usage. The team stops at the usage lines you set and carries on when there's room.

items: Research three summer trips, step 2 of 3

steps.title: The roadmap
steps.text: Every bigger idea goes on the roadmap first, with your own words, so nothing gets lost. Then it goes to the team when you're ready, or it gets planned for a time, like tonight at ten.

pieces.title: The mail check
pieces.line: HQ reads your new mail every hour

steps.title: Every hour, quietly
steps.text: Every hour HQ reads your new mail and keeps only what might need you. Very important things, like a bill with a date or someone waiting for your answer, you hear at the start of every call until you say it's sorted. HQ never sends mail: drafts at the most, you send them yourself.

items: Your parcel is on its way

pieces.title: Weather and rain alerts
pieces.line: The weather at a glance, a text before the rain

steps.title: The weather
steps.text: The weather where you are, at a glance. Tap it for the hours ahead, and turn on the rain alert: {donna} texts you before a shower comes and follows it as it moves.

pieces.title: Settings, and what HQ helps you with
pieces.line: Voices, Free, and switching features on or off

steps.title: Voices and sound
steps.text: Pick each agent's voice, your microphone and where her voice plays, and the soft thinking sound.

steps.title: Microphone and sound, quickly
steps.text: The microphone button is a shortcut to the same place: switch to your headphones or another microphone in two taps, also in the middle of a call.

steps.title: What HQ helps you with
steps.text: Every feature is a switch: the calendar, the to-do list, texts, the weather, travel by public transport, the mail check, your news, notes, the team's work, and Life coaching. Turn off what you don't use: its button goes away and the rest moves up. Driving to appointments starts off: it needs your own maps key.

steps.title: Life coaching
steps.text: With Life coaching on, a few calm sessions with {pepper} build your long-term vision, from three to five years out down to your ideal week, and HQ supports you with it every day. You give your vision its own name.

steps.title: Free
steps.text: Free is plain Claude with only the web: none of your files, nothing saved. Handy to show HQ to someone without showing your life.

pieces.title: Life coaching
pieces.line: Your long-term vision, one calm session at a time

steps.title: Your vision, layer by layer
steps.text: With Life coaching on, this button opens your map: from the life you want in three to five years, down to this year, a six-week game, your ideal week and this week. Each layer shows its checklist: what's answered, what's left for later and what's still open.

steps.title: One session per layer
steps.text: Start a layer and {pepper} calls about only that one, one question at a time, and writes your answers down in your own words. Short sessions, so nothing drifts off.

steps.title: Check-ins, with a red dot
steps.text: HQ keeps the moments to look back: every week, at the end of a game, and a bigger check-in every few months. When one is due the button gets a red dot. There's also a chat with {pepper} just for life coaching.

pieces.title: Your own news
pieces.line: Only the topics and sources you pick, read inside HQ

steps.title: Your own newspaper
steps.text: News shows only what you asked for: the topics you care about, from the sources you picked, without the noise. It's read about every hour, and kept apart from your mail.

steps.title: Set it up in a short call
steps.text: The first time, tap Set up your news: a short call about what you want to hear about, what to leave out, and where from. {donna} or {pepper} suggests free sources and checks them. Change it the same way any time.

items: Two science sites, one local paper

steps.title: Read it here
steps.text: Tap an item to read it inside HQ, with its source under it. A dot on the button means there's something new since you last looked.

pieces.title: Your six-week game
pieces.line: One simple game you can win, six weeks at a time

steps.title: A game you can win
steps.text: In Life coaching you design a six-week game with {pepper}: one simple thing, like moving every day. Once it's set up, this button shows it: where you are, the win line and how far along you are.

steps.title: Tick it off
steps.text: Tick today off here, or just say it on a call or text {donna}. Add how it felt or a note when you want. {donna} can nudge you in the evening if today's tick isn't in yet.

steps.title: Look back and keep it
steps.text: Every week you look back on it, and at the end there's a short debrief: was it fun, was it useful, what did you learn. Past games are kept, so you can open them again.

pieces.title: Make it yours
pieces.line: HQ is built to be expanded

steps.title: Your own headquarters
steps.text: This is the reason HQ was built in the first place: so everyone can have their own headquarters, with their work supported by their own team. What's in it now are the things its creator thought most people would want. His own HQ has many more, and people testing it have already built their own extensions.

steps.title: Customize, tailor, expand
steps.text: It's not limited to what you see here. Ask on a call for something new, give it to the team, and they build it into your HQ. Your own builds stay yours: updates never touch them.

steps.title: Updates never break your own
steps.text: What you add yourself is an extension: it lives in your own files, and an update never touches it. After every update HQ checks whether something you added might not fit the new version. If so, a short message says which one, with two buttons: talk it through with {donna}, or send it to your team to fix.

steps.title: Coming soon: shared best practices
steps.text: Ways of working that keep a build stable, like the checks that run every night and fix what broke, written so your own HQ understands them. Turn them on, and your HQ looks out for them and suggests them itself, so you don't have to be a programmer to avoid the classic mistakes.

facts: HQ runs on your own computer, on your own Claude plan, through Claude Code. Your voice is turned into text on your computer, and her voice is made there too; only the thinking goes to Anthropic, the same as any Claude chat.
Your phone reaches your computer privately (through Tailscale), with nothing open to the internet. Add the call page to your phone's home screen and it works like an app. There is also a Mac app.
Your own files live in your workspace, a folder of plain text files on your computer. They are never uploaded with HQ, and updates never touch them.
HQ is still in development, built and used daily by one person first, now shared with friends. A small grey version number opens what's new; an Update button appears when a new version is out.
The routine is a small helper that runs every minute without Claude, so it costs nothing while waiting. A watchdog brings things back when they stop.
Things that need your yes, like an appointment with other people in it or anything with your mail, are checked with you first. Mail is never sent.
After a real call, its transcript is saved and the call's notes go into your log, in your own words. Free calls and demo calls are never saved.

Travel on appointments uses open data, free and without a key: the live train, bus, tram and metro data the Dutch transport companies publish (through OVapi), the government's address service, and 9292 links. Driving is a separate feature, on your own Google Maps or TomTom key, kept on your computer; HQ ships no key and counts its looks, at most 150 a day.
